plan:
Hyperparam tuning name: activation_function. In this implementation, I will
modify the `RASModel` class to accept different activation functions as a
parameter during initialization. Additionally, I will iterate over a list of
activation functions, training the model with each function for hyperparameter
tuning. The experiment data will be structured according to the specified
requirements, and all relevant metrics will be saved in a single NumPy file at
the end of the training process.

Ablation name: Use of Multiple Synthetic Datasets. To implement the ablation
study using multiple synthetic datasets, I'll create three distinct datasets
with different label generation methods while maintaining a similar feature set.
Each dataset will be evaluated using the same model architecture and activation
functions to assess robustness across varying label relationships. The results
will be stored in an organized format for further analysis.

Ablation name: Dropout Regularization. To perform the ablation study on the
RASModel's performance with dropout regularization, I will modify the existing
model to include dropout layers after the first fully connected layer. I will
assess the performance of models with and without dropout across various
activation functions and save the results similarly to the original experiment,
ensuring to track metrics, losses, predictions, and ground truth values. By
mimicking the previous experiment structure, I aim to provide comparative
insights on the effect of dropout in the model architecture.

Ablation name: Feature Importance Removal. The proposed solution involves
modifying the baseline implementation to include an ablation study that
systematically removes one feature at a time from the dataset. For each
configuration, a model will be trained and evaluated to assess the impact of the
removed feature on the model's performance. The performance metrics (training
and validation losses) for each configuration will be collected and saved in a
structured format.

Ablation name: Variability of Input Features. The proposed solution involves
modifying the baseline code to implement an ablation study that evaluates the
impact of varying input feature counts (2, 4, and 6 features). This is achieved
by creating multiple synthetic datasets, each with a different number of
features, and training the model on each dataset while capturing metrics and
losses. The results will be saved as numpy arrays for later analysis.

Ablation name: Feature Scaling Ablation. The proposed solution involves creating
an additional experimental setup that examines the impact of feature scaling on
model performance. This will be accomplished by implementing two versions of the
synthetic dataset: one with the original feature generation (0 to 1) and another
without any modification (i.e., values randomly generated without scaling). The
code will train the model on both datasets and log relevant metrics for
comparison.

Ablation name: Activation Function Variability Across Layers. In this
implementation, I'll expand the previously defined neural network model to allow
for varying activation functions across the first and second layers. I'll create
combinations of different activation functions for each layer and evaluate the
model performance for each combination. The results, including training and
validation losses as well as metrics, will be saved according to the specified
format.

Ablation name: Input Noise Injection. The proposed solution introduces Input
Noise Injection to the existing model implementation. This modification will
involve adding Gaussian noise to the input features during training to evaluate
how the model performs when faced with perturbed data. The experiment will run
in a similar manner to the baseline, looping through activation functions while
capturing the effects of input noise on training and validation losses. Results
will be saved in a structured format for further analysis.

Ablation name: Multi-Dataset Evaluation. To implement the ablation study for
Multi-Dataset Evaluation, I will create three distinct synthetic datasets with
different relationships between features and labels. Each dataset will be
evaluated using the same model architecture with varying activation functions.
The results, including training/validation losses and metrics for all datasets,
will be stored in a structured manner. Finally, I will save this information as
a numpy array, ensuring that it follows the specified naming conventions.

Ablation name: Multi-Dataset Evaluation. To implement the ablation study for
Multi-Dataset Evaluation, I will generate three distinct synthetic datasets with
varying feature-label relationships. Each dataset will be created using a
different formula for label calculation to introduce diverse patterns. The
existing training and evaluation loop will be modified to accommodate the new
datasets, and relevant metrics, losses, predictions, and ground-truth values
will be collected and saved accordingly. This will allow us to analyze the
model's robustness and adaptability across multiple datasets.

Ablation name: Activation Merging at Output Layer. The proposed implementation
involves modifying the RASModel to include an ablation study for an "Activation
Merging at Output Layer" approach. This new method will compute the mean and
maximum activations from the last hidden layer before feeding them into the
final output layer. The model will be trained and evaluated similarly to the
original version, with results tracked in the experiment data structure. The
final metrics and losses will be saved using the specified naming convention.

The issue in the previous implementation was due to a reference to an undefined
variable, `features`, when attempting to add noise. This can be fixed by using
the `batch["features"]` tensor, which is already available and has been moved to
the appropriate device. Additionally, I will ensure that all required metrics
and loss tracking are updated and printed, along with appropriate saving of
these data at the end of training.

The issue in the previous implementation arises due to referencing the
`features` variable, which is only defined within the loop during batch
processing, outside its intended scope when adding noise for the input. To
resolve this, we can replace the `features` used in the noise addition line with
the `batch["features"]` directly. This ensures the model training operates
correctly by injecting noise into the correct input tensor.

Ablation name: Use of Batch Normalization. In this implementation, I will
introduce an ablation study to assess the impact of batch normalization in the
RASModel. I will create two variants of the model: one with batch normalization
after the fully connected layers and one without it. The training and evaluation
processes will be performed for both models, and the results will be saved in
the specified format for further analysis.

Ablation name: Multi-Dataset Evaluation with Feature Distribution Variance. The
solution involves creating three synthetic datasets with varying statistical
properties to conduct an ablation study on the model's robustness. Each dataset
will simulate different feature distributions by altering the means and
variances of the input features. The model will then be trained and evaluated
using these datasets, and the results, including metrics and losses for each
dataset, will be stored in a structured format for later analysis.

Ablation name: Dataset Size Variation. To implement the ablation study for
dataset size variation, we will modify the existing code to evaluate the model's
performance with varying sizes of the synthetic dataset (500, 1000, and 2000
samples). For each dataset size, we will create a new instance of the
`FeedbackDataset`, train the model, store the training and validation losses, as
well as the performance metrics. Finally, we'll save all the results in the
specified format.

Ablation name: Multiple Synthetic Dataset Evaluation. I will implement the
ablation study to evaluate the model's performance across multiple synthetic
datasets with varying distributions and complexities. This will involve creating
several datasets, each with different feature correlations and relationships to
the labels. The model will then be trained and evaluated on each dataset using
the same activation functions as before, with all relevant metrics and losses
saved in a structured format for future analysis.

To address the identified issues in the previous implementation, I will ensure
that the model's inputs and outputs are correctly normalized and properly moved
to the appropriate device (CPU or GPU). Additionally, I will introduce a metric
for Review Quality Score (RQS) to evaluate the quality of peer reviews in the
context of the experiment. This RQS will be computed based on predictions and
ground truth data, updating every epoch, and saved alongside the experiment
metrics. Lastly, I'll ensure that all data is saved correctly at the end of the
experiment.

Ablation name: Synthetic Dataset Variability. The proposed solution involves
modifying the `calculate_labels` method in the `FeedbackDataset` class to create
multiple synthetic datasets using different mathematical relationships. Each
dataset will be generated with varying constraints and functions to assess their
impact on model performance. During the training process, the model will be
evaluated for each dataset, and metrics such as losses and predictions will be
collected and saved for further analysis.

To resolve the issues in the previous implementation, I will ensure that both
the model and data tensors are correctly moved to the appropriate device
(CUDA/CPU) during preprocessing and training. Additionally, I'll enforce proper
normalization of input features to maintain numerical stability and improve
model training performance. Moreover, I will incorporate a new metric for Review
Quality Score (RQS) that will be updated during each epoch and saved at the end.
Lastly, I'll print the validation loss to monitor performance throughout
training.

Ablation name: Activation Function Depth Variation. The proposed solution
involves modifying the existing neural network model to support depth-specific
activation functions. Instead of applying a single activation function
throughout the model, we will allow for different activation functions at each
layer of the architecture. This will be achieved by passing a list of activation
functions to the model constructor, allowing the user to specify different
functions for each layer. The training loop will remain largely unchanged, but
with the updated model handling varying activations. We will save the results of
our ablation study according to the specified format.
